item.title: Optimal Polynomial Approximants vanishing arbitrarily close to the origin
item.description: arXiv:2611.26723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work concerns a sequence of stable polynomials on the bidisk whose affine optimal polynomial approximants in the Hardy space of the bidisk have zero varieties that come arbitrarily close to the origin.
item.dc:creator: Athanasios Beslikas, Christopher Felder, Douglas T. Pfeffer

item.title: A reciprocal-matrix proof of Sendov's theorem and applications to control theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.26766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This proof grew out of the author's research on interpreting mathematical statements from the viewpoint of control theory. Its value lies both in the understanding it brings and in the applications that arise from the argument. Let $a$ be a simple zero of a polynomial of degree $n\ge 2$ whose zeros lie in the closed unit disk. If $c_1,\ldots,c_{n-1}$ are its critical points, counted with multiplicity, then the reciprocals $1/(a-c_j)$ are the eigenvalues of an explicit matrix built from the other zeros. A failure of Sendov's bound at $a$ would therefore make the associated discrete-time system asymptotically stable. This observation leads to an alternative proof of the quadratic inequality of Tang and Zhang, including its equality case. Building on the reflection and centering arguments of Mazur, Tao and Zhang, we estimate the change in the integral of the derivative product when all the reciprocal displacements are replaced by their mean $s$. An exact pairwise cancellation bounds the difference in terms of the variance. For an interior zero rotated to $0<a<1$, the normalized trace $s$ determines a contour through $\overline{s}/a$. If the mean squared reciprocal distance is at most one, integration along this contour gives $(n-1)(2a\Re(s)-a^2)<20$. A uniform phase estimate and reflection at $1/a$ then rule out this possibility in every degree $n\ge 257$. A fourth-moment estimate treats degrees two through five. For degrees five through 256, three bounds derived from one polynomial moment identity exclude the full range of the two remaining real parameters by exact integer arithmetic. As an application, Sendov's theorem illustrates how differentiating the denominator of a closed-loop transfer function can increase robustness in discrete-time systems and decrease it in continuous-time systems. The proofs have been formalized in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Latchezar P. Tomov

item.title: Szeg\H{o} kernels and logarithmic flatness of K\"ahler metrics
item.description: arXiv:2611.27099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(L,h)$ be a positive Hermitian line bundle over a complex manifold $M$, inducing a K\"ahler metric $g$. We give a detailed account of the Hardy space and Szeg\H{o} kernel of the unit circle bundle of $(L^*,h^*)$ when $M$ is possibly noncompact. Assuming that $M$ admits a complete K\"ahler metric and that the Ricci curvature of $g$ is bounded below, we use the framework developed in our earlier work on Bergman logarithmic flatness to establish a diagonal expansion of the Szeg\H{o} kernel and characterize its logarithmic singularity in terms of the Tian--Yau--Zelditch--Catlin expansion of the Bergman kernels of $(L^k,h^k)$. This extends and answers a question of Lu--Tian. We introduce the notions of Szeg\H{o} and Bergman logarithmic flatness for K\"ahler metrics, not necessarily globally polarized, and prove that every compact locally homogeneous polarized metric is Szeg\H{o} logarithmically flat. For K\"ahler--Einstein metrics, we prove Szeg\H{o} logarithmic flatness implies Bergman logarithmic flatness. Examples arising from Bryant's metrics show that Bergman logarithmic flatness does not imply Szeg\H{o} logarithmic flatness.
item.dc:creator: Peter Ebenfelt, Ming Xiao, Hang Xu

item.title: Finite Angular Derivative Sets and Almost Isometries of the Hyperbolic Disc
item.description: arXiv:2611.27387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a subset $E$ of the unit circle is the set of points at which an analytic self-map of the unit disc has a finite angular derivative if and only if $E$ is an $F_\sigma$ set. We also prove that, for every countable dense subset $E$ of the unit circle, there exists an almost isometry in the sense of Garnett--Papadimitrakis whose angular derivative is finite precisely on $E$.
item.dc:creator: Angel Lorenzo

item.title: Weighted fixed-bidegree subelliptic estimates for the \(\overline{\partial}_f\)-Neumann problem on Lipschitz pseudoconvex domain
item.description: arXiv:2611.27502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish two types of \emph{a priori} subelliptic estimates for the twisted \(\overline{\partial}_f\)-Neumann problem on a bounded pseudoconvex domain with Lipschitz boundary. The estimates feature a subelliptic gain in \((0, 1/2)\) and are uniform with respect to the bidegree. The boundary is assumed to satisfy a plurisubharmonic-type condition, characterized by the local existence, near each boundary point, of a bounded plurisubharmonic function whose Hessian blows up algebraically near the boundary, with potentially different exponents at different points. The twisting function is holomorphic in a neighborhood of the domain, has bounded gradient, and its critical set inside the domain consists of isolated interior points with finite vanishing orders.
item.dc:creator: Ping'an Zhang

item.title: Local connectivity of Julia sets of Newton maps of trigonometric and hyperbolic functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.26654v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the Newton maps of $\sin z$, $\cos z$, $\sinh z$, and $\cosh z$, each of which is transcendental meromorphic and has infinitely many unbounded immediate attracting basins. We first verify directly that, for the cosine Newton map $N_{\cos}(z) = z + \cot z$, the half-planes $\{\pm \operatorname{Im} z > M\}$ are repelling petals at infinity for every $M \ge 2$. These explicit petals allow us to apply the tame-basin criterion of Bara\'nski, Fagella, Jarque, and Karpi\'nska and obtain local connectivity of the spherical boundary of each immediate basin of $N_{\cos}$. We also show that the Newton map of $Ae^{\lambda z} + Be^{-\lambda z}$, where $AB\lambda \neq 0$, is affinely conjugate to the sine Newton map $N_{\sin}(z) = z - \tan z$. The published local-connectivity theorem for $J(N_{\sin})$ therefore applies to this entire family, including the cosine and the two hyperbolic Newton maps. We describe the invariant lines and basin geometry of the four maps and illustrate the corresponding dynamical planes numerically.
item.dc:creator: Molla Basir Ahamed, Sayantan Chakraborty

item.title: Sparse Analytic Representation of Stationary Processes with Bounded Spectral Density
item.description: arXiv:2611.27152v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider centered second-order stationary processes Y={Y_t}{t\in R} with bounded spectral density S_Y and develop a sparse analytic representation framework. A nontrivial stationary process on the real line generally does not belong to L^2(\Omega,L^2(R)), since stationarity implies E||Y||{L^2(R)}^2=\infty. To overcome this infinite-energy obstruction, we replace the sample-path viewpoint by the bounded linear operator \widetilde Y: L^2(R) \to L^2(\Omega), with \widetilde Y(f) = \int_{R} \hat{f}(\xi) Z_Y(d\xi), where Z_Y is the orthogonal random measure in the spectral representation of Y. Applying \widetilde Y to Cauchy kernels in the upper and lower half-planes yields random analytic functions U_+ and U_-. For \alpha>1, we prove U_+ \in L^2(\Omega, B_\alpha^2(C^+)) and U_- \in L^2(\Omega, B_\alpha^2(C^-)), where B_\alpha^2(C^\pm) are weighted Bergman spaces. We combine U_+ and U_- into U(\omega,z) = U_+ for z \in C^+, and U_- for z \in C^-, and with B_\alpha = B_\alpha^2(C^+) \oplus B_\alpha^2(C^-), prove U \in L^2(\Omega, B_\alpha). We establish boundary vanishing, energy identity, and convergence, and derive covariance identities for the coefficients. In L^2(\Omega, B_\alpha), we apply stochastic pre-orthogonal adaptive Fourier decomposition (SPOAFD) to U_+ and U_- separately, using normalized reproducing kernels of the Bergman spaces as dictionaries. The adaptive selection is determined by the spectral density. Finally, using the Poisson kernel and SPOAFD expansions, we establish weak mean-square convergence of the original process against test functions in C_c^\infty(R).
item.dc:creator: Yiqiao Zhang, Fang Yang, Tao Qian

item.title: An affine surface with 3-step nilpotent fundamental group
item.description: arXiv:2611.27475v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a smooth complex affine surface $Y$ such that $\pi_1(Y)$ is virtually $3$-step nilpotent, but not virtually $2$-step nilpotent. This gives a negative answer to the quasi-projective version of Campana's nilpotency problem.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Polevoy, Vasily Rogov

item.title: Elementary Factorization For Continuous Orthogonal Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.27838v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every nullhomotopic continuous map, from a finite-dimensional normal topological space X to the complex special orthogonal group, is a product of elementary orthogonal matrices with entries in the ring of continuous functions. The number of factors is bounded by a constant depending only on the size of the matrices and the covering dimension of X. The same factorization result holds for nullhomotopic special orthogonal matrices with entries in a unital commutative Banach algebra.
item.dc:creator: Gaofeng Huang, Phan Quoc Bao Tran

item.title: One exponential or two? Invertibility tests for Jordan epimorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2611.27850v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How many exponential factors must one test to recognise a Jordan epimorphism? Let \(T\colon A\to B\) be a unital linear surjection between complex Banach algebras, with \(B\) semisimple. Using a spectral-isometry theorem of Aznay and Chabbabi, we show that it suffices for \(T\) to send every product of two exponentials to an invertible element to force $T$ to be Jordan. If only single exponentials are tested, \(T\) is a Jordan epimorphism if and only if its kernel is a two-sided ideal, or equivalently a left ideal. A resolvent estimate on a logarithmic spiral shows that a single exponential suffices when the source is a \(C^*\)-algebra or the group algebra \(\ell^1(G)\) of a discrete group. A separate argument, which does not use the spectral-isometry theorem, shows that a single exponential also suffices when the target is a \(C^*\)-algebra with a faithful family of tracial states.
item.dc:creator: Catalin Badea

item.title: The Thurston algorithm for general entire maps on the complex plane: Existence and uniqueness
item.description: arXiv:2611.27925v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that a marked topological entire Thurston map $(f,A)$ of stable parabolic type is Thurston equivalent relative to $A$ to a postsingularly finite entire function if and only if it has no Levy cycle relative to $A\cup\{\infty\}$. Here $A$ is a finite forward-invariant set containing the postsingular set. In the realizable case, the entire function is unique up to complex affine conjugacy, and every orbit of the Thurston pullback converges to its fixed point. We establish a Wolff--Denjoy type estimate for nonexpanding self-maps $T$ of the Teichm\"uller space of any connected orientable surface of finite type without boundary. If $T$ has an unbounded orbit, there are a nonzero measured foliation $G$ and a constant $C$ such that $\operatorname{Ext}_{T^k x}(G)\le C\operatorname{Ext}_x(G)$ for every $x$ and $k\ge0$. For a fixed-point-free transcendental Thurston pullback, this supplies the foliation used in the existence proof. A central tool is a fixed finite measure obtained as the total-variation limit of renormalized pushforward measures transported back along a Teichm\"uller ray. It allows us to select a cylinder at a late time and compare the mass of the same marked region at different times. If $G$ has a cylinder, a four-point extremal-length estimate and the Thurston matrix force a Levy cycle. Otherwise, in the absence of a Levy cycle, cluster rescaling shows that cylinders of large modulus carry almost all the fixed measure at all late times. Following a cylinder of definite mass until its modulus decreases gives a contradiction. We compare this geometric argument with the proofs for real entire maps and exponential maps.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian van Strien

item.title: Freedom is all you need
item.description: arXiv:2611.27943v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The functional calculus allows for the rigorous analysis of functions of matrices or even operators. The free functional calculus gives the natural class of functions over any category. We initiate the representation theory for taking a generic free functional calculus to the classical nc functional calculus going back to Taylor, Voiculescu and many others, with an eye towards learning of categories. The functional calculus on direct sum closed and locally similarity (i.e. change of coordinates) invariant domains inherits the niceties of complex analysis and large-scale parallel networks, such as automatic analyticity, free universal monodromy, which gives a hypothetical explanation for beneficial overfitting.
item.dc:creator: Julian Bushelli, James Eldred Pascoe

item.title: The K\"ahler-Ricci soliton on bounded pseudoconvex domains
item.description: arXiv:2412.03345v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we establish rigidity results for K\"ahler--Ricci solitons on bounded pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb C^n$. We first show that if a complete K\"ahler metric has $C^1$ quasi-bounded geometry and negatively pinched Ricci curvature outside a compact set, then any soliton vector field whose metric dual is closed must vanish. In particular, such a soliton is K\"ahler--Einstein. We then prove that any Bergman K\"ahler--Ricci soliton of bounded domains is K\"ahler--Einstein. Combined with Huang--Xiao's resolution of Cheng's conjecture, this yields a soliton analogue of Cheng's conjecture. We also provide several model domains as examples.
item.dc:creator: Zehao Sha

item.title: Weighted Kernel Functions on Planar Domains
item.description: arXiv:2508.14016v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the variation of weighted Szeg\H{o} and Garabedian kernels on planar domains with respect to the weight and establish a Ramadanov-type convergence theorem. As a consequence, we obtain detailed information on the behaviour of the zeros of the weighted Szeg\H{o} and Garabedian kernels for weights close to the constant function $1$ on the boundary. We also study the weighted Ahlfors map and strengthen known results concerning its boundary behaviour. Explicit examples of the weighted kernels are presented for certain classes of weights. We strengthen Nehari's construction of the weighted Szeg\H{o} and Garabedian kernels by showing that the meromorphic function associated with the weight can be chosen holomorphic. We further identify his auxiliary kernels with reproducing kernels of finite-codimensional Hardy subspaces, and derive further representation formulas and consequences. Finally, we discuss the weighted Carath\'{e}odory metric, and describe relations between the weighted Szeg\H{o} and Garabedian kernels with certain classical kernel functions.
item.dc:creator: Aakanksha Jain, Kaushal Verma

item.title: Affine balancing of complex dilatations: affine invariants and optimal distortion of harmonic quasiconformal mappings
item.description: arXiv:2609.37606v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Target real-affine postcomposition induces a disk automorphism on the complex dilatation of orientation-preserving planar harmonic mapping. Motivated by the lack of intrinsic distortion measures for real-affine orbits, we introduce the affine circumradius, affine diameter, and affine circumcenter from the hyperbolic geometry of the dilatation range. The affine circumradius is the logarithm of the minimal value of the maximal differential distortion over the real-affine orbit, and the affine circumcenter describes minimizers up to Euclidean similarity. For non-constant dilatation, at most two or three contact points determine the minimal enclosing hyperbolic disk. We prove sharp two-sided radius-diameter bounds, with equalities realized by globally univalent harmonic quasiconformal mappings. Each orbit admits a canonical balanced representative, for which we derive a sharp norm bound for the gap between the harmonic pre-Schwarzian derivative and that of its analytic part. This bound exhibits quadratic small-dilatation asymptotics, and the balanced representative achieves the minimal dilatation parameter over the real-affine orbit.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Gang Wang, Deguang Zhong

item.title: Normal Limits of the Squeezing Function and Strict Pseudoconvexity
item.description: arXiv:2611.16703v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $p$ be a boundary point of a bounded pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$, $n\ge2$, and suppose the squeezing function tends to $1$ along the inward normal at $p$. We show that $p$ is strictly pseudoconvex if the boundary is $C^{2,\alpha}$ near $p$ for some $0<\alpha\le1$, without assuming finite type or convexity. The proof begins under local $C^2$ regularity near $p$. A comparison of Bergman kernels rules out nonconstant holomorphic curve germs through $p$ contained in the boundary. With these curve germs excluded, rescaled normal translations give rise to a holomorphic semigroup. Classifying this semigroup identifies the normalized kernel limit at selected scales and yields the logarithmic growth exponent $n+1$ for the diagonal Bergman kernel along the inward normal. Under the $C^{2,\alpha}$ assumption, Levi degeneracy at $p$ would give a kernel upper bound with exponent strictly below $n+1$. This contradiction proves $p$ is strictly pseudoconvex.
item.dc:creator: Xiangsen Qin

item.title: Completely Regular Growth of Transcendental Entire Solutions to Linear Difference Equations with Polynomial Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.16865v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let \(f\) be a transcendental entire solution of order less than one of the linear difference equation \[ \sum_{j=0}^{m}P_j(z)\Delta^j f(z)=0, \qquad P_m\not\equiv0, \] where \(P_0,\ldots,P_m\) are polynomials. Applying the inverse Newton transform \(\mathcal S\), which maps the falling factorial \(z^{\underline n}\) to \(z^n\), we obtain a function \(g=\mathcal S f\) satisfying a nontrivial linear differential equation with polynomial coefficients. We further prove that the Newton transform preserves completely regular growth in the Levin-Pfluger sense. Consequently, \(f\) is of completely regular growth, and its zeros are regularly distributed. An example involving the Gamma function shows that the conclusion may fail for solutions of order 1. Finally, we provide examples of linear difference equations with entire coefficients that admit solutions which are not of completely regular growth, even when all the coefficients are themselves of completely regular growth.
item.dc:creator: Xuxu Xiang, Jianren Long, Mingjin Li

item.title: Hardy operators: In the footsteps of Brown, Halmos, and Shields
item.description: arXiv:2501.14706v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper discusses the two classical Hardy operators $\mathcal{H}_{1}$ on $L^2(0, 1)$ and $\mathcal{H}_{\infty}$ on $L^2(0, \infty)$ initially studied by Brown, Halmos and Shields. Particular emphasis is given to the construction of explicit cyclic and $*$-cyclic vectors in conjunction with a characterization of their invariant and reducing subspaces. We also provide a complete description of the frame vectors for $I - \mathcal{H}_{1}^{*}$.
item.dc:creator: Eva A. Gallardo-Guttierrez, Jonathan R. Partington, William T. Ross

item.title: Curvature rank, numerical dimension, and cohomology growth
item.description: arXiv:2610.09295v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $L$ be a holomorphic line bundle on a compact complex manifold $X$ of dimension $n$, and let $r$ be the least integer such that the first Bott--Chern class of $L$ is represented by a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form of rank at most $r$ at every point. For any nonzero coherent analytic sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ whose support has dimension $d$, we prove that $h^q(X,\mathcal F\otimes L^p)=O_\varepsilon(p^{r+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and every $0\le q\le d$. This is the exponent conjectured by Ma--Marinescu--Zelditch, up to an arbitrarily small loss. In the extreme degrees $q=0$ and $q=d,$ the bound can be taken to be $O(p^{\min\{r,d\}})$. If, moreover, $X$ is in Fujiki's class and $L$ is nef, then $h^q(X,\mathcal F\otimes L^p)=O(p^{\min\{\nu(L),\,d-q\}})$, where $\nu(L)$ is the numerical dimension of $L$. This answers a question of Demailly for compact Fujiki manifolds. Finally, for arbitrary $X$, any singular Hermitian metric \(h\) on \(L\) with semipositive curvature and analytic singularities, and any holomorphic vector bundle \(E\) on $X$, we have \(h^q(X,E\otimes L^p\otimes\mathcal I(h^{\otimes p}))=O_\varepsilon(p^{\min\{n-q,b+\varepsilon\}})\) for any $0\leq q\leq n$, where \(b\) is the maximum curvature rank outside the pole set of $h$, and $\mathcal I(h^{\otimes p})$ is the multiplier ideal sheaf. When $X$ belongs to Fujiki's class, the exponent is \(\min\{n-q,b\}\).
item.dc:creator: Xiangsen Qin
